title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
summary: For positive integers $s$ and $k$, the Ramsey number $r(s,k)$ is the minimum integer $n$ such that any graph on $n$ vertices contains a clique of size $s$ or an independent set of size $k$. We prove that for any fixed $s \ge 3$ and $k$ tending to infinity, the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers satisfy \[ r(s, k) \ge Ω\left(\frac{k^{s-1}}{(\log k)^{2s-4}} \right), \] which matches, up to polylogarithmic factors, the upper bound established over 90 years ago by Erdős and Szekeres.
